title: Maxi-DMEK and Maxi -Rebubbling- Maxi-DMEK and Maxi-Rebubbling – New concepts to ensure DMEK graft adhesion in unicameral eyes or nach glaucoma surgery
summary:
Background: DMEK is considered the best standard treatment for diseases of the innermost corneal layer (Spaniol et al., 2023; Melles 2006). In this surgery, the innermost layer of the cornea is replaced with a donor transplant. The donor transplant is pressed against the patient's cornea using only a gas bubble in the front part of the eye. It usually stays attached long-term, even after the gas bubble has dissolved. However, despite high success rates, there is a higher risk of the transplant detaching in eyes with complex eye diseases (for example, if the natural lens or iris is missing, or after glaucoma surgeries). This happens because there is not enough gas, or the gas moves too early into the back part of the eye or under the eye’s conjunctiva (Romano et al., 2024). In these cases, gas often has to be injected again ("rebubbling"). This leads to a greater loss of cells in the transplant and increases the risk that the transplant will fail (Cohen et al., 2021).

Research Question: Can the new surgical technique of filling both the front and back chambers with gas at the same time ("Maxi-DMEK" and "Maxi-Rebubbling") improve how well DMEK transplants stick in eyes with complex eye diseases?

Methods: Data will be taken from digital patient files and then anonymized (names are replaced by a list of numbers). This data was already collected during regular medical care by the staff at the eye clinic. The anonymized data will be analyzed statistically looking back at these past records.

interventions.name: Patients with corneal endothelial dysfunction who have already undergone a 'Maxi-DMEK' or 'Maxi-Rebubbling' procedure

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with corneal endothelial dysfunction previously treated with 'Maxi-DMEK' or 'Maxi-Rebubbling
Exclusion criteria:
the abscence of medical documentation
